https://www.mediafax.ro/english/educatio.text: Education union members refuse to participate in discussions on the new pay law The Federation of Free Education Unions (FSLI), the “Spiru Haret” Federation of Education Unions, and the “Alma Mater” National Trade Union Federation announced Thursday in a joint press release that they will not attend the discussions scheduled for today at the Ministry of Labor regarding the new pay law. The three federations state that they do not wish to legitimize, through their presence, a consultation they consider to be devoid of substance. “We will not use our presence to endorse a mere public relations exercise. The three federations have already conveyed their joint, well-founded, and detailed position during previous discussions. We cannot endorse stopgap solutions or minimal adjustments that do not genuinely address the problems we have highlighted. Given that the government and the Minister of Labor have already told us, bluntly and cynically, that this is the best they can do, our participation in today’s meeting would be completely pointless, serving only the public-image interests of those in power,” states the press release issued by the three labor federations. They accuse the current draft wage law of violating the regulations adopted by the government following the end of the 2023 general strike in education and argue that the government is not honoring the commitments it made to employees in the education system. “We draw attention to the fact that the current draft law flagrantly violates the very regulations adopted by the government upon the conclusion of the 2023 general strike. It is a display of hypocrisy and a total disregard for the commitments made to society. What the government is doing today is not only a violation of the law but a direct abandonment of the entire education system, proving once again that education is not a priority for the current government,” the education union representatives added. „Romanian lawmakers must choose between two options” In addition, the three federations are calling on Parliament to reject the current bill or to promote a version that reflects the importance of the work carried out by education personnel. “Romanian lawmakers must choose between two options: to refuse to introduce this pseudo-bill on salary reform or to promote a sound law in which education employees are classified according to the importance of the work they perform, as was the case with the draft developed by the Ministry of Labor in collaboration with World Bank representatives in 2024,” the joint statement further notes. On Tuesday, the judges of the Court of Appeals suspended the draft law on the remuneration of personnel paid from public funds, at the request of Sanitas. Thus, the draft published on July 17, 2026, can no longer be introduced or debated in Parliament. The judges found a clear appearance of illegality due to the lack of genuine consultation. In addition, the decision requires the government to resume official negotiations with public sector unions. The draft law on a unified pay scale is a reform that Romania has committed to under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR). https://www.romania-insider.com/antibiot.text: Energy Romania's Antibiotice Iași cuts electricity bill by 20% with own solar park 18 August 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Romanian state-controlled pharmaceutical producer Antibiotice Iași (BVB: ATB) reduced its electricity expenses by 20% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, following the use of its own photovoltaic generation, according to the company's H1 financial report submitted to the Bucharest Stock Exchange and cited by Economedia.ro . The company said its combined expenses for electricity, natural gas and drinking water fell to RON 11.68 million in the first six months of 2026, from RON 12.52 million a year earlier. Electricity costs accounted for most of the reduction in utility expenses. The photovoltaic plants generated savings of approximately 20% of the electricity consumed during the period, equivalent to RON 1.2 million based on the average purchase price from suppliers, Antibiotice said. Antibiotice commissioned a 2.5 MW photovoltaic park in 2024 following an investment of RON 11.8 million, financed through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) and the company's own contribution. The installation covers about 25% of the operating electricity needs of the company's industrial platform in Iași. The pharmaceutical producer also reported that electricity expenses associated with its electric vehicles were RON 76,000 lower in the first half of 2026 than at the end of June 2025. Industrial companies and local authorities in Romania have increasingly invested in photovoltaic generation to reduce electricity costs and increase energy autonomy, supported in part by European and government financing programmes. Photograph: Able Seaman Brenton Freind/Department of Defence Royal Australian Navy Video recording device found in cabin of HMAS Leeuwin navy ship in Cairns Defence announcement comes after Jacqui Lambie tells parliament a camera had been found concealed in a women’s shower on board Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Josh Butler Wed 14 Oct 2026 03.19 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 03.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A “video recording device” was found in the cabin of a Royal Australian Navy ship in Cairns, the defence department has revealed, just hours after senator Jacqui Lambie alleged in parliament that a camera had been found concealed in a women’s shower on the vessel. The department confirmed on Wednesday afternoon that a device had been found aboard the HMAS Leeuwin three days earlier. In a statement after Guardian Australia had contacted the department for response to Lambie’s allegations, a spokesperson said police were investigating, but did not reveal further details about where the device was located. “On 11 October 2026, Defence became aware that a video recording device had been located in the cabin of Royal Australian Navy ship HMAS Leeuwin, while alongside in Cairns, Queensland,” they said. “The incident was referred to the Joint Military Police Unit and Defence is working with civilian authorities. Defence takes this incident extremely seriously and does not tolerate unacceptable behaviour in any form.” Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email On Wednesday morning, Lambie – an ADF veteran and advocate for defence personnel – told the Senate that she’d been contacted by a former member of the navy with allegations about a camera being found aboard HMAS Leeuwin. “The sender told me that concealed cameras have recently been found in the female sailors’ showers facilities on the vessel HMAS Leeuwin, based in Cairns ,” she said in the Senate. “I was also told this had occurred recently and prevented the vessel from sailing while investigations were ongoing. Even more disturbing are claims that footage from these cameras may have been uploaded online before the cameras were discovered. View image in fullscreen Independent Senator Jacqui Lambie speaking to journalists at Parliament House. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP “How many of our female sailors have unknowingly been recorded in their most private moments? How much footage has been distributed online so far, retained or uploaded without knowledge or consent? These are the questions today I ask Navy.” Guardian Australia asked the department if any perpetrator had been identified, if the defence force was aware of hidden cameras being found in other navy facilities, and if any such footage from hidden cameras had been found to have been shared online. The department did not directly answer those questions. In its statement, it said HMAS Leeuwin had “remained alongside to enable the investigation and ensure immediate support was provided to members of the ship’s crew”. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Spying device detectors may give domestic abuse victims false sense of security, study finds Read more “The welfare of individuals remains Defence’s priority, and support is ongoing. As the matter is currently under investigation and to protect the privacy of the affected individuals, Defence is unable to provide further comment at this time,” it said. Asked at a subsequent press conference about the incident, Lambie said she was unhappy with the department’s response. “Defence needs to know this. Your people had a gutful, and if there was abuse going on, they’re now coming to me. OK, I’m right on their tail. Enough is enough. Get control of what is going on in the defence force,” she said. “What I want to know is, have they gone around on the rest of those boats, the subs, whatever, and had a look and make sure there’s no other cameras? Because we are not sure whether it’s coming from contractors that go on them, or whether it’s come from defence members.” Explore more on these topics Royal Australian Navy Australian military Cairns Jacqui Lambie Queensland news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Labor’s bill to cut private health insurance rebate blocked by Greens over pensioner carve-out Ben Roberts-Smith attends Canberra event honouring Australian troops who served in Afghanistan What started as a small political spot fire turns into a major irritant for the PM and his treasurer Australian army soldier killed and five others injured in training exercise in the Northern Territory Hegseth calls US-built nuclear submarines the ‘apex predator’ of the seas. Photograph: Joshua Bratt/PA London Four-year-old girl dies after falling from east London tower block Police say the incident at an address in Barking is not believed to be suspicious Charlie Moloney Sun 25 Oct 2026 19.25 GMT Last modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 19.38 GMT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A four-year-old girl has died after falling from a tower block in east London . She was injured after “falling from height” at an address in St Paul’s Road, Barking, on Saturday and died in hospital, the Metropolitan police said. The force said investigations were still being carried out but “at this time, the incident is not believed to be suspicious”. Officers were called on Saturday at 11am. A police spokesperson said: “Officers attended the scene alongside the London ambulance service, where emergency first aid was administered. “The girl, aged four, was taken to hospital but, very sadly, later died from her injuries. Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with the child’s family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time. “An investigation into the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident is ongoing. However, at this time, the incident is not believed to be suspicious.” A spokesperson for the London ambulance service said it sent ambulance crews, a clinical team manager, an incident response officer, an advanced paramedic practitioner and London’s air ambulance to the scene. “We treated a child at the scene before taking the patient to a London major trauma centre,” the ambulance spokesperson said. Anyone with information about the incident has been asked to contact police on 101.
